name: Carol Dunn
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember working near home for one unusually easy month.” On Saturday, near Ferris Deli, Carol asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I thought all six of us wanted a bus. One wants his license back and another wants work nearer her dad.
appearance: Carol has one cheek that creases before the other. Look for short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a cream pullover with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. In conversation Carol draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first.
personality: Carol is cheerful on a bad morning and unexpectedly melancholy after a success. Finishing a hard thing means losing the daily company of the people who worked on it.
agenda: To let each rider name what would make the arrangement unnecessary.
family: Chloe Briggs is Carol’s stepsibling. Carol brings the paper and a pen. Chloe decides what stays off the paper. They have helped each other make decisions that were far easier to discuss once the figures could be moved around. The decisions themselves still belong to the person asking. Asked about *The understudy sings*, Chloe says, “I promoted the show around one voice. I put the understudy's full name on every remaining poster.”
connections: Patricia Ramos. One person wants a rider-owned rota. The other wants each rider to have a way out.

reactions.response: Carol checks whether waiting will make the whole shift late and tells the rider the decision.
